registers.name: CLKCTRL
registers.title: Generic Clock Control
notes: Write CLKCTRL as one 16-bit access carrying the configuration and ID. To read it, first write the generic clock's ID to CLKCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read CLKCTRL.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Writing it locks the generic clock named by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator named by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor against further writes, until a power reset. Generic clock generator 0 cannot be locked.

values.text: Generic clock, its generator and division factor unlocked.
Generic clock, its generator and division factor locked.

fields.name: CLKEN
fields.text: Turns the generic clock on or off.

fields.name: GEN
fields.text: Generic clock generator feeding this generic clock.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Names the generic clock that the rest of CLKCTRL configures. A power reset returns CLKCTRL to its reset value for every ID, the RTC included; a user reset does so only for an ID other than the RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0. After a power reset GEN, CLKEN and WRTLOCK are 0x00 for every ID except the WDT, whose GEN is 0x02, whose CLKEN follows the WDT Enable bit of the NVM User Row (0x01 when it is one, 0x00 when zero) and whose WRTLOCK follows the WDT Always-On bit of the NVM User Row the same way. After a user reset WRTLOCK never changes; for the RTC, GEN and CLKEN become 0x00 when WRTLOCK and CLKEN are both 0 and are kept otherwise; for the WDT with WRTLOCK at 0, GEN becomes 0x02 and CLKEN follows the WDT Enable bit as after a power reset, and with WRTLOCK at 1 both are kept; for every other ID, GEN and CLKEN become 0x00 when WRTLOCK is 0 and are kept when it is 1.

values.name: GCLK_DPLL_32K

registers.name: GENCTRL

fields.name: RUNSTDBY

values.text: Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO level follows GENCTRL.OOV.

fields.name: DIVSEL
fields.text: Chooses how the generator divides its clock source. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV 0 or 1.

fields.name: OE

values.text: Output on its GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.

fields.name: OOV

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Selects which generic clock generator is configured or read. A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, the RTC's generator included, to 0x00010600 for generator 0, 0x00010302 for generator 2 and the ID alone (0x0000000n) for generators 1, 3, 4 and 5. A user reset gives generator 0 the same value, and generators 1-5 too unless the RTC clock or a generic clock with WRTLOCK at 1 runs from them, in which case they keep their contents.

registers.name: GENDIV
registers.title: Generic Clock Generator Division
notes: Write GENDIV as one 32-bit access carrying the division factor and ID. To read it, first write the generator's ID to GENDIV.ID with an 8-bit access, then read GENDIV.

fields.name: DIV
fields.text: Division factor for the selected generator. Width depends on the generator: generator 0 has 8 bits (DIV[7:0]), generator 1 has 16 (DIV[15:0]), generator 2 has 5 (DIV[4:0]), generators 3-8 have 8 (DIV[7:0]); writes to higher bits are ignored.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Selects the generic clock generator the division factor applies to. A power reset resets GENDIV for every ID, the RTC's generator included, to DIV 0 with the ID (0x0000000n). A user reset does the same for generator 0, and for generators 1-5 unless the RTC clock or a generic clock with WRTLOCK at 1 runs from them, in which case they keep their contents.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the compare x interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

values.text: Compare x interrupt on; the CMPx flag raises a request.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the overflow interrupt enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the synchronization-ready interrupt enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the compare x interrupt enable; writing 0 does nothing. Reads the enable state.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE1

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter overflows; requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Set when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless the fall came from enable or software reset; requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Set one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter matches compare x; requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.CMPx is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while registers are being synchronized between the clock domains, and 0 once that is done.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 0 halts the RTC in debug mode; 1 lets it keep running. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Direction of the frequency correction.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Size of the correction made to the RTC prescaler; 1 to 127 sets how far the RTC frequency is adjusted.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Current value of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: PER
fields.text: Period value of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: COMP
fields.text: 16-bit compare value, checked against COUNT all the time; on a match INTFLAG.CMPn sets on the following counter cycle.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC to give the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT; not synchronized. 0x0 DIV1 through 0xA DIV1024 divide by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024 in turn; 0xB-0xF reserved.

fields.name: MATCHCLR
fields.text: Clears the counter on a Compare/Alarm 0 match; used in Mode 0 and Mode 2 only, writable only while the RTC is disabled, not synchronized.

values.text: Counter kept on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.
Counter cleared on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: CLKREP
fields.text: Picks the hour format of the CLOCK register; used in Mode 2 only, writable only while the RTC is disabled, not synchronized.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects how the RTC runs; not synchronized. 0x0 COUNT32 is Mode 0, a 32-bit count; 0x1 COUNT16 is Mode 1, a 16-bit count; 0x2 CLOCK is Mode 2, time and date; 0x3 is reserved.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off; the written value reads back at once, STATUS.SYNCBUSY is set until the change takes effect, then cleared. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the RTC; it overrides any other write in the same operation. Writing 0 does nothing. CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY clear once the delayed reset finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Writing 1 starts synchronization of the register named by READREQ.ADDR and sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RCONT
fields.text: Writing 1 keeps the register named by READREQ.ADDR synchronized on every update and stops READREQ.RREQ from clearing by itself; writing 0 stops it. Cleared by a write to the register named by READREQ.ADDR.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Offset of the register to read-synchronize; only COUNT and CLOCK, at one shared address, can be, so this is fixed read-only at 0x10.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Overflow event output enable.

fields.name: ALARMEO0
fields.text: Alarm 0 event output enable.

values.text: An event on every Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: PEREOx
fields.text: Periodic interval x event output enable, one bit for each of x = 0 to 7.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Overflow interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on; a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Synchronization Ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Synchronization Ready interrupt on; a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the Alarm 0 interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Alarm 0 interrupt on; a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Overflow interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Synchronization Ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Alarm 0 interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE2

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an overflow, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1; writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Set when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless the fall came from enable or software reset; raises an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Set on the CLK_RTC_CNT cycle following an ALARM0 match, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.ALARM0 is 1; writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while registers are being synchronized between the clock domains, 0 once that is done.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 1 lets the RTC keep running in debug mode; 0 halts it there. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Direction of the frequency correction.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much the RTC prescaler is corrected; a value of 1 to 127 adjusts the RTC frequency in step with that value.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years counted from a reference year chosen by software; a year with YEAR[1:0] = 0 is a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 for January up to 12 for December.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 up to 28, 29, 30 or 31 by month and year.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour: 0 to 23 when CTRL.CLKREP is 0; when it is 1, HOUR[3:0] runs 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM. Codes listed: 0x0-0xF reserved, 0x10 PM, 0x11-0x1F reserved.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

registers.name: ALARM
registers.title: Alarm n Value - MODE2
notes: ALARM0 is compared continuously with CLOCK, under the mask in MASKn.SEL. A match sets INTFLAG.ALARM0 one counter cycle later and, with CTRL.MATCHCLR at 1, also resets the counter to zero.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Alarm year; compared only when MASKn.SEL is 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Alarm month; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Alarm day; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Alarm hour; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Alarm minute; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Alarm second; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 0.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which parts of Alarm n take part in the match. 0x0 OFF: alarm off; 0x1 SS: seconds; 0x2 MMSS: seconds and minutes; 0x3 HHMMSS: adds hours; 0x4 DDHHMMSS: adds days; 0x5 MMDDHHMMSS: adds months; 0x6 YYMMDDHHMMSS: adds years; 0x7 reserved.

values.name: DDHHMMSS
values.text: Seconds, minutes, hours and days compared.

values.name: MMDDHHMMSS
values.text: Seconds, minutes, hours, days and months compared.

fields.name: LVLENx
fields.text: Set: requests at priority level x go to the arbiter; clear: requests at that level are ignored. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Level x requests are not served.

fields.name: CRCENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the CRC module on. Write 0 turns it off only while CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY is 0; with CRCBUSY at 1 the write is ignored. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the DMAC on. A 0 written during a transfer takes effect, aborting the transfer, only once the internal transfer buffer has emptied, which happens when the current burst finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 while DMAENABLE and CRCENABLE are both 0 to return every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value; with either enabled the request is ignored and the access returns an error. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Picks what feeds the CRC: 0x0 NOACT nothing, 0x1 IO the I/O bus, codes 0x2-0x1F reserved, 0x20-0x3F CHN a DMA channel n, with 0x21-0x3F also given as reserved. Held fixed while a CRC is running (shown by CRCBUSY) until it finishes or the CRC module is turned off. With a DMA channel as source, that channel signals when the CRC is done.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: CRC polynomial: 0x0 CRC16 (CRC-CCITT), 0x1 CRC32 (IEEE 802.3), 0x2-0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of each bus access when the CRC takes data from the I/O interface: 0x0 BYTE, 0x1 HWORD half-word, 0x2 WORD, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data word to run through the CRC. The cycles until the new checksum is ready depend on CRCCTRL.CRCBEATSIZE; each byte takes one clock cycle.

registers.name: CRCCHKSUM
registers.title: CRC Checksum
notes: Holds the 16- or 32-bit checksum produced by the CRC.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The computed CRC; read it only with CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY at 0. For CRC-16 the upper 16 bits read 0 and the value is the checksum; for CRC-32 the value is the checksum bit-reversed (bit 31 swapped with bit 0, bit 30 with bit 1, and so on).

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a CRC finishes with a checksum of zero; goes to 0 when a new CRC source is chosen.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: CRC running. With the I/O interface as source (CRCSRC 0x1): set by a write to CRCDATAIN, cleared by writing 1. With a DMA channel as source (CRCSRC 0x20-0x3F): set when that channel is enabled, cleared when it is disabled, and a written 1 does nothing. Writing 0 never does anything.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Whether the DMAC keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves this bit as it is.

values.text: DMAC stops with the halted CPU.
DMAC keeps running while the CPU is halted.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority while moving data: 0x0 DISABLE background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH latency-critical.

fields.name: FQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority while fetching descriptors: 0x0 DISABLE background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH latency-critical.

fields.name: WRBQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority while writing back: 0x0 DISABLE background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH latency-critical.

fields.name: SWTRIGx
fields.text: Write 1 to trigger channel x from software when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; if PEND is already 1 the bit is just set. Cleared when the channel's CHSTATUS.PEND goes to 1, by writing 1 to it, or by writing 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 3.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 3 (RRLVLEN3 = 1): number of the level-3 channel most recently granted access. With static priority (RRLVLEN3 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n outranks channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Kept when RRLVLEN3 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 2.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 2 (RRLVLEN2 = 1): number of the level-2 channel most recently granted access. With static priority (RRLVLEN2 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n outranks channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Kept when RRLVLEN2 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 1.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 1 (RRLVLEN1 = 1): number of the level-1 channel most recently granted access. With static priority (RRLVLEN1 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n outranks channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Kept when RRLVLEN1 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Arbitration scheme for channels at priority level 0.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 0 (RRLVLEN0 = 1): number of the level-0 channel most recently granted access. With static priority (RRLVLEN0 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n outranks channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Kept when RRLVLEN0 is written to 0.

registers.name: INTPEND
registers.title: Interrupt Pending
notes: Shows the lowest-numbered DMA channel with an interrupt pending.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Suspend interrupt pending; writing 1 clears that channel's Suspend flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Complete interrupt pending; writing 1 clears that channel's Transfer Complete flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Error interrupt pending; writing 1 clears that channel's Transfer Error flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt pending, valid while SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is 1; updated when a lower channel gains a pending interrupt or when the software clears a channel's interrupt sources, and reads 0 when none is pending. Writing it opens indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINTx
fields.text: 1 while channel x has an interrupt pending; goes to 0 when channel x's interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHx
fields.text: 1 from when channel x starts a transfer until its trigger action finishes, a bus error is seen on it, or it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCHx
fields.text: 1 while a transfer waits on channel x; goes to 0 when the channel's trigger action starts executing, a bus error is seen on it, or it is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count of the transfer now running, kept in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back memory when the arbiter grants another channel. Valid only while ABUSY is 1.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: 1 from when the next descriptor's transfer count is read out of write-back memory until the running count has been stored back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel held in the active channel registers, updated each time the arbiter grants a channel.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: 1 while a trigger request from a level-x channel is executing or pending.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Start address of the descriptor memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Start address of the write-back memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel the channel registers act on; write it before reading or writing any channel register.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the channel on. A 0 written during a transfer takes effect, aborting the transfer, only once the internal transfer buffer has emptied, which happens when the current burst finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 while ENABLE is 0 to return the channel's registers to their reset values; ignored while ENABLE is 1. Clears itself when the reset is done. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel: 0x0 NOACT none, 0x1 SUSPEND suspend the channel, 0x2 RESUME resume it, 0x3 reserved. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: What one trigger starts: 0x0 BLOCK a block transfer, 0x1 reserved, 0x2 BEAT a beat, 0x3 TRANSACTION a whole transaction.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts the channel's transfer: 0x00 DISABLE software or event triggers only, 0x01 SERCOM0 RX, 0x02 SERCOM0 TX, 0x03 SERCOM1 RX, 0x04 SERCOM1 TX, 0x05-0x0B reserved, 0x0C TC1 overflow, 0x0D TC1 match/compare 0, 0x0E TC1 match/compare 1, 0x0F TC2 overflow, 0x10 TC2 match/compare 0, 0x11 TC2 match/compare 1, 0x12 ADC result ready.

values.name: DISABLE
values.text: No peripheral trigger; software or event only.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Arbitration level of the channel; a higher level wins over a lower one: 0x0 LVL0, 0x1 LVL1, 0x2 LVL2, 0x3 LVL3 (levels 0 to 3), 0x4-0x7 reserved. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event output; an event is produced for each condition chosen by the descriptor's BTCTRL.EVOSEL. Present only on channels that have an event output.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event input. Present only on channels that have an event input.

values.text: Incoming events do not run the channel event action.
Each incoming event runs the channel event action.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an incoming event, only while EVIE is 1; only on channels with an event input: 0x0 NOACT none, 0x1 TRIG starts a transfer or a periodic transfer, 0x2 CTRIG starts a transfer if its condition holds, 0x3 CBLOCK block transfer under a condition, 0x4 SUSPEND suspends the channel, 0x5 RESUME resumes it, 0x6 SSKIP skips the next block suspend action, 0x7 reserved.

values.name: TRIG
values.text: Event triggers a transfer, or periodic transfers.

values.name: CTRIG
values.text: Event is a conditional transfer trigger.

values.name: CBLOCK
values.text: Event allows a conditional block transfer.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Event skips the next block suspend action.

registers.name: CHINTENCLR
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Disables channel interrupts without a read-modify-write; its bits mirror CHINTENSET.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. With the block action set to none, a finished block transfer does not set the TCMPL flag.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Channel Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTENSET
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Enables channel interrupts without a read-modify-write; its bits mirror CHINTENCLR.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Channel Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with the suspend block action finishes, a software suspend command runs, a suspend event arrives, or the DMAC fetches an invalid descriptor. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block transfer finishes and its block action includes the interrupt. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set when a bus error occurs during a beat or the DMAC fetches an invalid descriptor. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared when a software resume command runs.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: 1 from when the channel starts a transfer until its trigger action finishes, a bus error occurs, or the channel is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: 1 while a transfer waits on the channel; goes to 0 when its trigger action starts executing, a bus error occurs, or the channel is disabled.

registers.name: BTCTRL
registers.title: Block Transfer Control
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number x 0x10.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Address step, applied to the source or destination address as STEPSEL picks: next address = address + BEATSIZE x factor, with 0x0 X1, 0x1 X2, 0x2 X4, 0x3 X8, 0x4 X16, 0x5 X32, 0x6 X64, 0x7 X128.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Which address takes the STEPSIZE step: 0x0 DST the destination, 0x1 SRC the source.

values.name: DST
values.text: Step size is used on the destination address.

values.name: SRC
values.text: Step size is used on the source address.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: 1: the destination address advances, by 1 by default, or by STEPSIZE when STEPSEL is 0. 0: it stays fixed through the transfer.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: 1: the source address advances, by 1 by default, or by STEPSIZE when STEPSEL is 1. 0: it stays fixed through the transfer.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of one beat, the bus access for one data move, for both reads and writes: 0x0 BYTE 8 bits, 0x1 HWORD 16 bits, 0x2 WORD 32 bits, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does when a block finishes: 0x0 NOACT nothing, 0x1 INT block interrupt with the channel carrying on, 0x2 SUSPEND suspend the channel, 0x3 BOTH suspend and block interrupt.

values.name: INT
values.text: Block interrupt; the channel carries on normally.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: Block interrupt and the channel is suspended.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: When the channel puts out an event: 0x0 DISABLE never, 0x1 BLOCK a strobe at each finished block, 0x2 reserved, 0x3 BEAT a strobe at each finished beat.

values.name: BLOCK
values.text: Event strobe at each completed block transfer.

values.name: BEAT
values.text: Event strobe at each completed beat transfer.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: Marks the descriptor usable; a 0 here in descriptor or write-back memory suspends the channel when it fetches this descriptor. Cleared by hardware in write-back memory when the channel is aborted, an error occurs in the block, or the block finishes.

registers.name: BTCNT
registers.title: Block Transfer Count
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number x 0x10.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit count of beats in the block. During a transfer the internal counter drops by 1 per beat and is written to the channel's write-back memory when the channel loses priority, is suspended or is disabled (by finishing, by a transfer error or by software).

registers.name: SRCADDR
registers.title: Transfer Source Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number x 0x10.

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address of the block's last beat.

registers.name: DSTADDR
registers.title: Transfer Destination Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number x 0x10.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address of the block's last beat.

registers.name: DESCADDR
registers.title: Next Descriptor Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number x 0x10.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: SRAM address of the next descriptor, 128-bit aligned. A value of 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. The written value reads back at once and STATUS.SYNCBUSY goes to 1; the change takes effect after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY returns to 0.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EIC register to its reset value and turn the EIC off; it overrides any other write in the same access. The reset finishes after synchronization, when SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both return to 0. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; 0 once that is done.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Edge or level the NMI responds to: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set when the NMI pin meets the NMISENSE condition, and raises an interrupt request. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTEOx
fields.text: Turns on the event from pin EXTINTx, produced at each detection.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Disables interrupts without a read-modify-write; its bits mirror INTENSET.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Write 1 to disable external interrupt x; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Enables interrupts without a read-modify-write; its bits mirror INTENCLR.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Write 1 to enable external interrupt x; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Set when pin EXTINTx meets its sense condition; requests an interrupt when the matching INTENCLR/SET.EXTINT[x] bit is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUPENx
fields.text: Lets pin EXTINTx wake the device from sleep when it meets its sense condition.

values.text: EXTINTx does not wake the device.

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.title: Configuration n
notes: The heading for FILTENx leaves out bit 3, the diagram's FILTEN0.
The heading for SENSEx leaves out bits 2:0, the diagram's SENSE0.
Also listed under the name CONFIG0.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT7.

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT7 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN6
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT6.

fields.name: SENSE6
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT6 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN5
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT5.

fields.name: SENSE5
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT5 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN4
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT4.

fields.name: SENSE4
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT4 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN3
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT3.

fields.name: SENSE3
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT3 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN2
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT2.

fields.name: SENSE2
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT2 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN1
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT1.

fields.name: SENSE1
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT1 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN0
fields.text: Filter enable for EXTINT0.

fields.name: SENSE0
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT0 raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 NONE no detection, 0x1 RISE rising edge, 0x2 FALL falling edge, 0x3 BOTH either edge, 0x4 HIGH high level, 0x5 LOW low level, 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Key that lets the command in CMD run: 0xA5 is the execution key. Any other key blocks the write and sets STATUS.PROGE, which is also set when an earlier command has not finished. Write the key in the same access as CMD, and only while READY is one. When an APB command meets an AHB access in the same cycle, the AHB access goes first and the command runs once the AHB bus and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads one until the command has been issued.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Selects the command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erase Row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write Page: copies the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.

values.name: EAR
values.text: Erase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: WAP
values.text: Write Auxiliary Page: copies the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: LR
values.text: Lock Region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlock Region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: PBC
values.text: Page Buffer Clear: empties the page buffer.

values.name: SSB
values.text: Set Security Bit: writes 0x00 to the first byte of the lockbit row, setting the security bit.

fields.name: CACHEDIS
fields.text: Turns the NVM cache off.

fields.name: READMODE
fields.text: How the cache handles misses: 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY adds no wait states on a miss, for the highest system performance; 0x1 LOW_POWER lowers cache power but adds a wait state on every miss, which stalls the CPU and can lengthen run time; 0x2 DETERMINISTIC makes a hit and a miss take the same time, set by the flash wait states, for code needing fixed timing; 0x3 is reserved.

values.name: NO_MISS_PENALTY
values.text: No wait state on a cache miss; best system performance.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Lower cache power, with a wait state on every cache miss.

values.name: DETERMINISTIC
values.text: Hit and miss take the same time, set by the flash wait states.

fields.name: SLEEPPRM
fields.text: NVM power reduction during sleep: 0x0 WAKEONACCESS puts the NVM block in low-power mode on entering sleep and wakes it on its first access; 0x1 WAKEUPINSTANT puts it in low-power mode on entering sleep and wakes it on leaving sleep; 0x2 is reserved; 0x3 DISABLED turns automatic power reduction off.

values.name: WAKEONACCESS
values.text: Low-power on entering sleep; wakes on first access.

values.name: WAKEUPINSTANT
values.text: Low-power on entering sleep; wakes on leaving sleep.

fields.name: MANW
fields.text: Chooses whether a page write starts on its own or only by command; this covers main memory and auxiliary rows.

values.text: A write to the page buffer's last word starts a write to the page given by the last written address.
Page writes start only by a command in CMD.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Wait states inserted on an NVM read, from 0 to 15, one per count; resets to 0. Software may change it to suit the NVM access time and the system clock frequency.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: Page size: 0x0 8 bytes, 0x1 16, 0x2 32, 0x3 64, 0x4 128, 0x5 256, 0x6 512, 0x7 1024 bytes. A given device family may not offer every size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: How many pages the main NVM address space holds.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A one disables the ERROR interrupt; a zero changes nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: A one disables the READY interrupt; a zero changes nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: A one enables the ERROR interrupt; a zero changes nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: A one enables the READY interrupt; a zero changes nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes to one on any NVME, LOCKE or PROGE error; writing one to it clears it.

values.text: No error since it was last cleared.
One or more errors since it was last cleared.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: NVM ready.

values.text: Controller busy with a program or erase.
Controller can take a new command.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Security bit status.

fields.name: NVME
fields.text: NVM error flag; writing one to it clears it.

values.text: The NVM controller has reported no program or erase error since the flag was last cleared.
The NVM controller has reported one or more errors since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: LOCKE
fields.text: Lock error flag; writing one to it clears it.

values.text: No locked region has been programmed since the flag was last cleared.
A locked region has been programmed since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: PROGE
fields.text: Programming error flag; writing one to it clears it.

values.text: No bad command or key has been written to the command register since the flag was last cleared.
A bad command, a bad key or both have been written to the command register since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: LOAD
fields.text: Goes to one as soon as one or more words are loaded into the NVM page buffer, and stays one until the page is written or the buffer is cleared by the PBCLR command; writing one to it also clears it.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Shows whether the NVM is in power reduction mode. It enters that mode by command or on entering sleep with SLEEPPRM chosen for it, and leaves it on an AHB access to the NVM block, by the SPRM and CPRM commands, or on leaving sleep with SLEEPPRM chosen for it.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: 16-bit hardware address given to the NVM when CMDEX runs a command; shift a byte address right by one before writing it. Updated by itself on page buffer writes and writable by hand; holds the offset within the addressed section.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: One lock bit per region; they are set and cleared only through commands in CMD.

registers.name: DIRn
registers.title: Data Direction
notes: Also listed under the name DIR.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of each I/O pin of the PORT group, one bit per pin.

registers.name: DIRCLRn
registers.title: Data Direction Clear
notes: Also listed under the name DIRCLR.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: A one clears that pin's bit in DIR, making the pin an input; a zero changes nothing.

registers.name: DIRSETn
registers.title: Data Direction Set
notes: Also listed under the name DIRSET.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: A one sets that pin's bit in DIR, making the pin an output; a zero changes nothing.

registers.name: DIRTGLn
registers.title: Data Direction Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name DIRTGL.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: A one flips that pin's bit in DIR, swapping its direction; a zero changes nothing.

registers.name: OUTn
registers.title: Data Output Value
notes: Also listed under the name OUT.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: Level each pin drives when DIR makes it an output; for an input pin with PULLEN on, it picks the pull direction.

values.text: Output low, or input pulled down.
Output high, or input pulled up.

registers.name: OUTCLRn
registers.title: Data Output Value Clear
notes: Also listed under the name OUTCLR.

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: A one clears that pin's bit in OUT: an output pin drives low, and an input pin with PULLEN on is pulled down. A zero changes nothing.

registers.name: OUTSETn
registers.title: Data Output Value Set
notes: Also listed under the name OUTSET.

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: A one sets that pin's bit in OUT: an output pin drives high, and an input pin with PULLEN on is pulled up. A zero changes nothing.

registers.name: OUTTGLn
registers.title: Data Output Value Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name OUTTGL.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: A one flips that pin's bit in OUT: an output pin's level inverts, and an input pin with PULLEN on swaps its pull direction. A zero changes nothing.

registers.name: INn
registers.title: Data Input Value
notes: Also listed under the name IN.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Level seen by each pin's input sampler: zero for a low pin, one for a high pin.

registers.name: CTRLn
registers.title: Control
notes: Also listed under the name CTRL.

fields.name: SAMPLING
fields.text: Input sampling mode for pins that DIR makes inputs. Samplers turn on and off eight pins at a time, so a pin asking for continuous sampling makes every pin in its byte sampled continuously.

registers.name: WRCONFIGn
registers.title: Write Configuration
notes: Also listed under the name WRCONFIG.

fields.name: HWSEL
fields.text: Which 16-pin half of the 32-pin group the atomic write configures; always reads zero.

fields.name: WRPINCFG
fields.text: A one writes the given DRVSTR, SLEWLIM, ODRAIN, PULLEN, INEN, PMUXEN and PINMASK values into PINCFGy of every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; a zero changes nothing. Always reads zero.

fields.name: WRPMUX
fields.text: A one writes the given WRCONFIG.PMUX value into PMUXn of every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; a zero changes nothing. Always reads zero.

fields.name: PMUX
fields.text: Value put into PMUXn of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPMUX is one; always reads zero.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Value put into PINCFGy.DRVSTR of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is one; always reads zero.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Value put into PINCFGy.PULLEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is one; always reads zero.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Value put into PINCFGy.INEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is one; always reads zero.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Value put into PINCFGy.PMUXEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is one; always reads zero.

fields.name: PINMASK
fields.text: Picks the pins to configure inside the half chosen by HWSEL, one bit per pin; always reads zero.

fields.name: PMUXO
fields.text: Peripheral function of odd-numbered pin 2n+1 of the PORT group when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is one: 0x0-0x7 pick functions A to H. Some codes may not be valid for a given pin.

fields.name: PMUXE
fields.text: Peripheral function of even-numbered pin 2n of the PORT group when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is one: 0x0-0x7 pick functions A to H. Some codes may not be valid for a given pin.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Drive strength of a pin used as an output.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal pull-up or pull-down of a pin used as an input.

values.text: Pull off; the input floats at high impedance.
Pull on; the input sits at a set level with nothing driving it.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Input buffer of the pin, whether input or output. With it off, the pin's real state cannot be read back.

values.text: Buffer off; the input is not sampled.
Buffer on; the input is sampled when needed.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Hands the pin's direction and output level to the peripheral chosen in PMUXn. At zero, DIR and OUT control the pin and PMUXn is ignored; at one, the chosen peripheral controls it, and IN still shows the pin's state if PINCFGy.INEN is one.

values.text: Multiplexer off; PORT registers set direction and output level.
Multiplexer on; the chosen peripheral sets direction and output level.

fields.name: GCLKREQ
fields.text: Whether each channel's generic clock runs continuously or only on demand from an event. Events on asynchronous paths need no generic clock.

values.text: Clock requested only when an event is detected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A one returns every EVSYS register to its reset state, and any other write in the same access is dropped; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: EDGSEL
fields.text: Edge detection on the channel for the synchronous and resynchronized paths: 0x0 NO_EVT_OUTPUT gives no event output, 0x1 RISING_EDGE detects rising edges, 0x2 FALLING_EDGE falling edges, 0x3 BOTH_EDGES both edges of the generator's signal. Must be zero on the asynchronous path.

values.name: NO_EVT_OUTPUT
values.text: No event output (synchronous or resynchronized path).

values.name: RISING_EDGE
values.text: Rising edge only (synchronous or resynchronized path).

values.name: FALLING_EDGE
values.text: Falling edge only (synchronous or resynchronized path).

fields.name: PATH
fields.text: Path the channel uses: 0x0 SYNCHRONOUS, 0x1 RESYNCHRONIZED, 0x2 ASYNCHRONOUS, 0x3 reserved. The channel's source can limit which paths are allowed.

fields.name: EVGEN
fields.text: Event generator connected to the channel.

rows: RTC compare 0 in modes 0 and 1, alarm 0 in mode 2.

fields.name: SWEVT
fields.text: A one fires a software event on the channel given by CHANNEL.CHANNEL; write it with CHANNEL.CHANNEL in one 16-bit access. A zero changes nothing; always reads zero.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel to configure or read.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel feeding the event user, written as channel number plus one: 0x0 selects no channel, 0x1-0x5 select channels 0-4, higher codes are reserved.

fields.name: USER
fields.text: Event user to tie to a channel, or whose channel is read back.

fields.name: CHBUSYx
fields.text: One while some user connected to channel x has yet to take a pending event; zero when the channel is idle.

fields.name: USRRDYx
fields.text: One when every user connected to channel x is ready for its events; zero while any of them is not.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: A one disables the channel x event detected interrupt; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: A one disables the channel x overrun interrupt; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: A one enables the channel x event detected interrupt; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: A one enables the channel x overrun interrupt; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Goes to one on the CLK_EVSYS_APB cycle after an event passes through channel x, raising an interrupt if EVDx is enabled; never set on an asynchronous path. Writing one clears it; a zero changes nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Goes to one on the CLK_EVSYS cycle after an overrun on channel x, raising an interrupt if OVRx is enabled; never set on an asynchronous path. Writing one clears it; a zero changes nothing.

peripherals.name: SERCOM USART
peripherals.title: SERCOM Universal Synchronous and Asynchronous Receiver and Transmitter

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Selects which end of a character leaves the data register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: In synchronous mode, selects which XCK edge changes TxD and which samples RxD. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Selects asynchronous or synchronous operation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Selects the frame format. Not synchronized.

values.text: Auto-baud with parity: break detection and auto-baud.

fields.name: SAMPA
fields.text: Selects which over-sampling clocks the receiver samples on; the set depends on CTRLA.SAMPR (16x or 8x). Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXPO
fields.text: Selects the SERCOM pad that receives data (RxD). Not synchronized.

fields.name: TXPO
fields.text: Selects the pads for TxD and XCK, and for RTS and CTS. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPR
fields.text: Selects over-sampling and baud-rate generation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Selects when STATUS.BUFOVF is set after a buffer overflow.

values.text: Set at the overflow's place in the data stream.
Set at once when the overflow happens.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Behaviour in standby sleep. Not synchronized. 0: with external clock, the clock is disconnected once the ongoing transfer ends and reception is dropped; with internal clock, the generic clock stops once the ongoing transfer ends and Receive Start or Transfer Complete can wake the device. 1: with external clock, Receive Start or Receive Complete wakes the device; with internal clock, the generic clock runs in all sleep modes and any interrupt can wake the device.

rows: Once the current transfer ends, the external clock is cut off and nothing more is received.
The generic clock stops after the current transfer; the device wakes on the Receive Start or Transfer Complete interrupt.
A Receive Start or Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock keeps running in every sleep mode; any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects USART operation of the SERCOM; write 0x0 or 0x1. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change has synchronized. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to put every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL back to its reset value and disable the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. It overrides any other write in the same access. While the reset runs, register writes give an APB error and reads return reset values; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear when it is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off, empties the receive buffer and clears STATUS.FERR, PERR and BUFOVF. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled it sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the receiver is on, after which the bit reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver on, or turns on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on or off. Writing 0 takes effect only after ongoing and pending transmissions finish. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled it sets SYNCBUSY.CTRLB until the transmitter is on, after which the bit reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Transmitter on, or turns on when the USART is enabled.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Selects even or odd parity when CTRLA.FORM enables parity. The transmitter adds the parity bit to each frame; the receiver checks it and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENC
fields.text: Selects the data encoding. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SFDE
fields.text: Lets the start-of-frame detector wake the device when a start bit arrives on RxD; the effect depends on INTENSET.RXS and INTENSET.RXC. Not synchronized.

values.text: Detection on; RXC wakes the device from all sleep modes.
Detection on; RXS wakes the device from all sleep modes.
Detection on; RXC and RXS both wake the device from all sleep modes.

fields.name: COLDEN
fields.text: Turns collision detection on (1) or off (0). Not synchronized.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Selects how many stop bits are sent. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Selects the number of bits per character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FP[2:0]/BAUD
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud value, used with fractional baud-rate generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1); sets the clock generation.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Baud value that sets the clock generation: bits 15:0 with arithmetic baud-rate generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=0), bits 12:0 with fractional (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1).

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: With IrDA encoding (CTRLB.ENC=1), sets the shortest pulse the IrDA receiver accepts: pulse length ≥ (RXPL + 1) × serial engine clock period.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Error interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Break interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Break interrupt is off.
The Receive Break interrupt is on.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the interrupt on a CTS input change; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Clear To Send Input Change interrupt is off.
The Clear To Send Input Change interrupt is on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Start interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Start interrupt is off.
The Receive Start interrupt is on.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Receive Complete interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Complete interrupt is off.
The Receive Complete interrupt is on.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Transmit Complete interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Transmit Complete interrupt is off.
The Transmit Complete interrupt is on.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Data Register Empty interrupt enable and turn the interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Data Register Empty interrupt is off.
The Data Register Empty interrupt is on.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Error interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Break interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Break interrupt is off.
The Receive Break interrupt is on.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the interrupt on a CTS input change; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Clear To Send Input Change interrupt is off.
The Clear To Send Input Change interrupt is on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Start interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Start interrupt is off.
The Receive Start interrupt is on.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Receive Complete interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Receive Complete interrupt is off.
The Receive Complete interrupt is on.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Transmit Complete interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Transmit Complete interrupt is off.
The Transmit Complete interrupt is on.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Data Register Empty interrupt enable and turn the interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: The Data Register Empty interrupt is off.
The Data Register Empty interrupt is on.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set on any error that has its own STATUS flag: COLL, ISF, BUFOVF, FERR or PERR. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Set when a break character arrives with auto-baud selected in CTRLA.FORM. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Set when the CTS pin changes. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Set when a start condition appears on RxD with start-of-frame detection on (CTRLB.SFDE=1). Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Set while DATA holds unread data; cleared by reading DATA or turning the receiver off. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Set when the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and DATA holds nothing new. Cleared by writing 1 or by writing new data to DATA; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Set when DATA is empty and can take new data; cleared by writing DATA. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Set when a collision is seen with collision detection on (CTRLB.COLDEN). Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ISF
fields.text: Set when auto-baud is selected (CTRLA.FORM) and a sync field other than 0x55 arrives. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTS
fields.text: With flow control on (CTRLA.TXPO), reads the CTS pin's present level. Writes do nothing.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Set on a buffer overflow: the receive buffer is full, a character waits in the receive shift register and another start bit arrives. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when the received character's first stop bit is 0. Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PERR
fields.text: Set on a parity mismatch with parity checking on (CTRLA.FORM 0x1 or 0x5). Read before DATA, it gives the status of the next character. Cleared by writing 1 or turning the receiver off; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Set from a write to CTRLB while the SERCOM is enabled until that write has synchronized; writing CTRLB again while it is set gives an APB error.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set from a write to CTRLA.ENABLE until enabling or disabling has synchronized; meanwhile a write to any register other than CTRLA.SWRST is dropped and gives an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set from a write to CTRLA.SWRST until the reset has synchronized; meanwhile any register write is dropped and gives an APB error.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: A read returns the receive data register, valid once INTFLAG.RXC is set; read STATUS first to get that character's errors. A write loads the transmit data register, to be done only while INTFLAG.DRE is set.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Selects whether the baud-rate generator runs while an external debugger halts the CPU.

values.text: Keeps running while the debugger halts the CPU.
Stops while the debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Selects which end of a character leaves the data register first. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL

fields.name: CMD

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Set when the slave has finished sending or receiving a byte. Hardware clears it on a write to DATA, a read of DATA in smart mode, or a valid command written to CMD; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Set when the address logic has received a valid matching address. Hardware clears it when CTRLB.CMD is written; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing. On clearing, ACK or NACK goes out as CTRLB.ACKACT says.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Set when a STOP is seen for a transaction the slave is in; a STOP between the master and another slave does not set it. Hardware clears it once a command is given on the next address match; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Set when the slave sees a START followed by a master code. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing. A STOP also clears it.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set when the slave SCL low extend time-out runs out. Cleared by answering a new START with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD = 3), by clearing INTFLAG.AMATCH, or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: 1 while the slave holds SCL low to stretch the clock; it is set along with INTFLAG.DRDY or INTFLAG.AMATCH and clears when that flag clears. Treated as read-only.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Set when the SCL low time-out runs out. Cleared by answering a new START with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD = 3), by clearing INTFLAG.AMATCH, or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SR

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Set when the slave could not drive a high data bit or a NACK; it then lets go of SDA and SCL at once and waits for its next address. Meant for SMBus address resolution; outside that, a collision is a protocol violation to handle as a bus error. It raises no interrupt. Cleared by answering an address match with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD = 0x3), by clearing INTFLAG.AMATCH, or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: No collision on the last byte sent.

fields.name: ERROR

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Set when a byte has been received in master read mode with no lost arbitration or bus error; the master then holds SCL low. SCL is let go and SB clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid command in CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears SB, but the transaction waits for one of those actions; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Set when a byte has been sent in master write mode, bus error or lost arbitration or not; also set when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in master read mode, and when a START is issued with the bus state unknown. Unless arbitration was lost, the master then holds SCL low. SCL is let go and MB clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid command in CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears MB, but the transaction waits for one of those actions; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Set when a DMA transaction uses automatic length and the slave answers NACK before the master has written ADDR.LEN bytes. Write 1 to clear; a write to ADDR also clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set when the slave SCL low extend time-out runs out. Write 1 to clear, which normal use does not need; a write to ADDR also clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set when the master SCL low time-out runs out. Write 1 to clear, which normal use does not need; a write to ADDR also clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: 1 while the master holds SCL low to stretch the clock; it is set along with INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB and clears once that flag clears and the following operation starts. Treated as read-only; writes do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Set when the SCL low time-out runs out. Write 1 to clear, which normal use does not need; a write to ADDR also clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Bus state as the master sees it. 0x0 Unknown: waits for a STOP or for software to force idle. 0x1 Idle: waiting for a transaction to start. 0x2 Owner: this master owns the bus. 0x3 Busy: another master owns the bus. The state is unknown once the master is enabled and while it is disabled. In the unknown state, writing 0x1 forces idle; no other state can be forced. Writing idle sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY.

values.name: Unknown
values.text: Master does not know the bus state; it waits for a stop condition or for software to force the bus idle.

values.name: Idle
values.text: Bus waits for a transaction to start.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Whether the slave acknowledged the last address or data byte sent. Writes do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Set when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a START or repeated START the master issues; INTFLAG.MB sets with it. Cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Set on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (a START straight followed by a STOP, say), or a time-out within a frame. When this master owns the bus, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB set too. Cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SYSOP
fields.text: Synchronization of a write to CTRLB, STATUS.BUSSTATE, ADDR or DATA while the SERCOM is enabled: set on the write, back to 0 once synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Synchronization of CTRLA.SWRST: set when SWRST is written, back to 0 once synchronized. While it is 1, a write to any register is dropped and gives an APB error.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: Number of bytes in a DMA transaction, 0 to 255. Used when ADDR.LENEN is 1; after LEN bytes have been sent or received, a NACK (on a master read) and a STOP go out on their own.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Turns on 10-bit addressing; may be written together with ADDR to send a 10-bit or a 7-bit address.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Turns on High-speed mode for this transfer, from repeated START to STOP; may be written together with ADDR.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: Turns on automatic transfer length.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Writing an address starts bus activity according to bus state. Unknown: the operation ends at once, with STATUS.BUSERR and INTFLAG.MB set. Busy: the master waits for idle. Idle: the master sends a START and the address; on an ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. Owner: the master sends a repeated START, after first sending the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this is done while INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is 1. The whole address is sent whether arbitration is won or lost; after a loss only ones go out. A write clears the flags INTFLAG.SB, INTFLAG.MB, STATUS.ARBLOST and STATUS.BUSERR. Reading ADDR never disturbs the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Reads the received byte or takes the byte to send. Valid only while the master holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD = 1), except a read of the last byte after the STOP has gone out. An access starts bus activity set by CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access type, read or write. Outside smart mode an access needs no synchronization.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Set when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless an enable or software reset caused it; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: Set one GCLK_ADC cycle after the window monitor condition is met; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.WINMON is 1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: Set when RESULT is overwritten before the CPU has read the previous value; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.OVERRUN is 1. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Set when a conversion result is ready; requests an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.RESRDY is 1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains, 0 once that is done.

fields.name: RESULT
fields.text: Conversion result, up to 16 bits. Single-ended without averaging gives 12 bits: with CTRLB.LEFTADJ set they sit in [15:4], so the high byte alone gives an 8-bit result; without it they sit in [11:0]. With oversampling the result fills [15:0] as AVGCTRL sets.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Lower threshold of the window monitor, when it is enabled.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Upper threshold of the window monitor, when it is enabled.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: Gain error correction applied to the result before it is stored, when CTRLB.CORREN is 1. Fixed point with 1 integer bit and 11 fraction bits, from 0.10000000000 to 1.11111111111 binary (1/2 up to but not including 2).

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: Offset error correction, two's complement, applied to the result before it is stored, when CTRLB.CORREN is 1.

fields.name: BIAS_CAL
fields.text: Bias calibration from production test; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration area to reach the specified accuracy.

fields.name: LINEARITY_CAL
fields.text: Linearity calibration from production test; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration area to reach the specified accuracy.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Whether the ADC keeps running in debug mode. Changeable only while the ADC is disabled, and to be written only when no conversion is in progress.
